mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a flattening industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND INDPRO flat for 2 months (change < 0.5%)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a concurrent supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate hiring, which in turn leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% indicates strengthening manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO acceleration above 1.5% is not followed by positive S&P 500 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent fall in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a statistical artifact or data inconsistency rather than genuine labor market strength; under such conditions, S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days are expected to be negative due to heightened uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls AND UNRATE falls in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such artifact months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the effective federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% during a period of negative GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an emergency easing cycle, which supports risk assets and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% indicates a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST outperformance is not followed by positive S&P 500 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid month-over-month increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) exceeding 5% coincident with a decline in consumer spending (proxied by GDPC1) suggests households are saving rather than spending, which typically precedes a consumer-driven pullback in equities and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes.
